deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch page preparing the topos-theoretic 'mapping cone' of the next page, done here in the setting of small categories and presheaves.

On the next page Grothendieck considers a morphism of topoi f : X_0 -> X_1. He views it as a topos fibred over Delta_1 and forms the total topos X = C(f). Its sheaves are triples (F_0, F_1, u) with u : f^*F_1 -> F_0. In X, X_0 is open, X_1 is the complementary closed subtopos, the gluing functor is f_*, and the closed inclusion i_1 : X_1 -> X is 'cohomologically trivial': H^*(X, F) ~ H^*(X_1, i_1^*F).

This page is the combinatorial analogue.
(1) Setup. A is a small category fibred or cofibred over a base: the cograph or cylinder of a functor, written 'int_A^p : A -> A_0', i.e. A is a Grothendieck integral of p. Next to it are the inclusion A_b -> b\A of a fibre into the comma category, and a small diagram of arrows over a transition morphism p : b_0 -> b'. These are the ingredients for computing p_{A!} (left Kan extension along A -> base) fibrewise via comma categories. The display p_{A!}(F) <- p_{A!} i_!(i^*F) compares pushing forward F with pushing forward its restriction.
(2) Formal lemma. If i : A_0 -> A has a left adjoint j (a retraction), then on presheaf categories i_! = j^* and i^* = j_*. This is the standard fact that u -| v implies v_! ~ u^* and u^* ~ v_* ... more precisely u^* -| v^*. One therefore gets the triple i_! -| i^* -| i_* : A_0^ <-> A^.
(3) Desired statements. He writes i_! i^* F ~ F and F ~ i_* i^* F, i.e. 'i^* pleinement fidèle', with i_* and i_! described as 'localisations'.
(4) The true weaker statement. Under 'Ex', he writes that F -> i_* i^* F induces an isomorphism on Gamma and on H^*. This is the presheaf version of the cohomological triviality of the closed piece. It holds because a functor i with a left adjoint is final in the strong sense: each comma category a\i has an initial object, hence is contractible. So i is aspherical (Grothendieck's terminology), and lim_{A^op} F = lim_{A_0^op} i^*F holds in all degrees.
(5) The underlined phrase 'i est tot. 0-asph.' (reading uncertain) names the needed hypothesis: i is (totally) 0-aspherical, i.e. 0-connected comma categories, for Gamma; aspherical for all H^n.

Purpose: to set up the dictionary 'morphisms of topoi <-> recollements', and to check that the mapping-cone/cylinder retracts cohomologically onto its closed end, first for categories, then for topoi.
errors: The isomorphisms i_! i^*F ~ F and F ~ i_* i^*F for ALL presheaves F would make i^* (= j_*) fully faithful. Together with i fully faithful and j -| i, this forces j to be fully faithful, so i is essentially an equivalence. As stated in general the claim is too strong. It can only hold for a restricted class of F, e.g. F inverting the arrows inverted by j. The correct general statement is the weaker one he writes next: the map induces isomorphisms on Gamma and on cohomology.

The bracketed list ('i^* pl. fid.; i_* localisation; i_! localisation') is only notes. Which functor is fully faithful versus a localisation depends on which adjoint exists, and this is not settled on the page.

ideas.what: For an adjunction u -| v between small categories, v_! ~ u^* and u^* -| v^*, hence u^* ~ v_* ... specifically here i_! = j^* and i^* = j_* when j -| i
A functor with a left adjoint is aspherical, so restriction along it preserves cohomology of presheaves

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine scratch computations: Kan extensions along an adjoint pair, and asphericity of a functor with an adjoint. They prepare a mapping-cone construction that is close to known recollement theory.
transcription_corrections: 'i_! = j^*' on top: the first line is cut off, but 'i_! = j^*' is consistent with the computation (j a left adjoint of i).
In the bracket, the first struck symbol is a scribble, not 'A'.
'iso sur Γ pour H F' plausibly reads 'iso sur Γ, (aussi) pour H^* F'.
'i et A tot 0-asph.' is plausibly 'i est tot. 0-asph.' (i totally 0-aspherical).
